title: Patient Informed Consent for Laboratory Test Orders: Questions and Answers
content:
The rule: Laboratory Test Orders of a class that requires informed consent may not be collected or tested until the patient has signed the informed consent. The consent is signed by the patient personally (a parent or legal guardian signs for a minor); the agent cannot sign or attest it. A consent remains valid for collection for the class's consent-validity period in calendar days from the date it was signed. The signing date is day 0 and the last day is included. A consent older than that must be signed again before collection.

**Q. Which orders does this cover?**
A. Orders of any service class whose settings require signed informed consent before testing. For those orders, neither collection nor testing may take place until the consent is signed.

**Q. Who may sign?**
A. The patient personally, or a parent or legal guardian for a minor patient. The agent cannot sign the consent and cannot attest that it was signed.

**Q. How long does a signature last?**
A. For the class's consent-validity period, counted in calendar days from the signing date as day 0, the last day included. A collection on the last day is covered; a collection on the following day needs a new signature first.

**Q. Worked boundary (hypothetical validity of V days, consent signed on day 0).**

| Collection on | Consent valid for this collection? |
|---|---|
| Day V | Yes (the last day is included) |
| Day V plus 1 | No; the consent must be signed again before collection |
